newsitem.title: UK: Storehouse says Xmas sales up 9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Storehouse says Xmas sales up 9 pct.

text.p: British retail group Storehouse Plc said on Friday group sales on a like-for-like basis rose by nine percent in the six weeks to Christmas Eve (December 24).
Total group sales in the period were up by 18 percent.
The company said same business sales were up 7.6 percent in the 40 weeks to January 4, 1997 and cumulative group sales up 15 percent including Childrens World, bought in May 1996.

Storehouse also said it appointed Christopher Martin, BHS finance director, to the board as group finance director. He replaces Dick Steele who has resigned from the board but will remain with the company until July.

In the six weeks to Christmas, sales at Bhs were up almost 12 percent, with same stores contributing 7.5 percent and new stores three percent. Franchise sales accounted for 1.5 percent, with sales of gifts and menswear particularly strong, Storehouse said.
British sales at Mothercare were slightly higher than the year-earlier period but overall sales were down by 0.8 percent because of the timing of shipments to overseas stores.
Same store sales at Mothercare were down four percent and Childrens World sales were down two percent, chiefly because of lower toy sales, Storehouse said.

"Bhs had a successful Christmas, with sales almost precisely to plan. Mothercare was disappointing but trading since Christmas, especially the new childrenswear ranges, has been more encouraging," group chief executive Keith Edelman said.
